analysis.title: Investing Through Disruption – Why Durability Matters More in Today's Environment
key_insights: SGA argues the market is rewarding growth that is not always durable. AI infrastructure build-out has concentrated leadership in a narrow group of perceived near-term beneficiaries, widening the gap between favored growth and growth backed by steadily compounding earnings.

SGA frames its approach as 'growth bond investing': quality businesses with durable growth, bond-like earnings predictability, meaningful participation in up markets and reduced drawdown exposure. It says its portfolios are not designed to maximize upside capture in every environment.

Per SGA, the AI rally is two rallies. Hyperscaler spending flows to higher-quality 'tier-one' franchises and to a less durable 'spillover layer' of lower-quality operators benefiting from temporary capital flows and scarcity value. SGA owns tier-one names and avoids spillovers, accepting some near-term relative-performance cost.

SGA says recent markets favored high-beta, cyclical and high-momentum stocks, amplified by speculative margin leverage, mega-cap concentration and retail momentum trading. Rate volatility compressed multiples on long-duration cash flows regardless of quality. This pressured SGA's relative returns (and peers') over the last 24 months.

SGA says its portfolios trade near their steepest relative discount to indexes since inception. Relative FY1 P/E is shown at its most attractive level since inception. It cites similar de-ratings in 1999, 2007 and early 2021, which narrowed when leadership broadened.

The Global Growth strategy breakdown: perceived AI beneficiaries (45% weight) had 40% y/y EPS growth and +50% share price return. Perceived AI losers (20% weight) had 40% EPS growth and -35% return. Other durable compounders (35% weight) had 5% EPS growth and -10% return. Examples: Nvidia, Broadcom, TSMC; Salesforce, SAP, Adyen; Visa, Danaher, HDFC Bank.
Over 5-year, 3-year and 1-year periods, SGA shows multiple compression weighing on returns, with valuation contributing negatively while earnings contributed positively.

SGA says forward earnings growth expectations for MSCI ACWI remain above long-term averages and near post-recession snapback levels, but consensus points to moderation into 2027 and 2028. It says relative performance has historically strengthened when growth expectations moderate and leadership broadens.

SGA flags a possible unwind of crowded positioning in cyclical AI beneficiaries and says it has seen early signs of a momentum reversal. It argues the AI-capex assumptions need only be questioned, not break, to cause repricing, citing the durability of AI hardware capex, circular financing and the timing of returns on invested capital.

The report shows an impending deceleration in hyperscaler capex growth (Empirical Research Partners data, as of 5/31/2026) and margin debt at elevated levels (FINRA, as of 8/31/2026), labeled as increased optimism and risk appetite.

Equinix (EQIX) is the featured case study: the largest global interconnection company with network effects, supply-constrained metro facilities, high switching costs and pricing power. SGA calls AI capex an accelerant, not the long-term thesis.

Case studies in the appendix are American Express, Disco, Equinix, Fast Retailing, Nu Holdings, NVIDIA, Salesforce and Waste Management. SGA contrasts the market's perceived risk with its durability argument for each, with estimated 3-year EPS growth of 11% to 27%.
Downside protection claim: across 20 significant 10%+ drawdowns, SGA portfolios beat benchmarks in 80% of cases with average downside capture of 77%.

Performance through 9/30/26 is weak against benchmarks. US LCG net YTD 2026 is 0.1% vs Russell 1000 Growth 15.7%... see key_data_points; Global Growth net 1-year is -4.7% vs MSCI ACWI 16.8%; Emerging Markets Growth net 1-year is -11.5% vs MSCI EM 29.2%.
earnings_insights: SGA reports the earnings growth of its portfolio companies versus benchmarks, based on non-GAAP operating earnings: SGA Global 15.1% vs ACWI 1.0%, U.S. 12.2% vs R1G 4.5%, International 16.1% vs ACWI ex-US 9.2%, Emerging Markets 16.7% vs MSCI EM 6.3%. These are since-inception averages through 2025, in the order of the report's chart labels.

Earnings variability (standard deviation of annual EPS growth, since inception through 2025) is shown as 7.1% vs 24.4%, 10.3% vs 41.2%, 8.7% vs 10.2% and 8.4% vs 23.2%, mapped by chart order to SGA vs benchmark.
Estimated 3-year EPS growth for case-study companies (SGA estimates): Amex 14%, Disco 19%, Equinix 16%, Fast Retailing 11%, Nu Holdings 24%, NVIDIA 27%, Salesforce 16%, Waste Management 13%.

risk_factors: A reset in AI monetization expectations.
Questioning of AI hardware capex durability, circular financing, and timing and magnitude of ROIC.
Unwind of crowded positioning and margin leverage in cyclical AI beneficiaries.
Continued underperformance of durable-growth strategies if narrow, momentum-driven leadership persists. SGA cannot predict when the market will recognize value.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler AI capex, AI monetization confidence and investors' willingness to pay elevated multiples support momentum leaders, and forward earnings growth remains above long-term averages.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus growth is moderating into 2027 and 2028 and hyperscaler capex growth is set to decelerate. Margin leverage and crowded positioning could unwind, and SGA says the assumptions need only be questioned to cause repricing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If growth expectations stay elevated and keep moving higher, momentum persists and SGA's thesis is delayed.

theme_stances.key_argument: Durable compounders trade at the steepest relative discount to indexes since inception while earnings keep compounding, and prior de-ratings narrowed when leadership broadened.
theme_stances.evidence: portfolios now trading near their steepest relative discount to indexes since their respective inception

theme_stances.key_argument: Momentum leadership relies on continued hyperscaler capex and AI monetization confidence, which need only be questioned to trigger repricing.
theme_stances.evidence: those assumptions need not break outright to matter

contextual_mentions: AI infrastructure build-out concentrating market leadership
relative P/E discount at inception-high levels
